question: What was India's annual exponential growth rate as per the 2011 Census?
solution:
The correct answer is **1**__**.64**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The annual exponential growth rate of India's population as per the 2011 Census is **1.64%**.
 
• This growth rate is a measure of how quickly the population is increasing each year.
 
• It is calculated using the formula for exponential growth: *P(t) = P₀ * ert*, where *r* is the growth rate.
 
• The growth rate reflects both natural increase (births minus deaths) and net migration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exponential Growth Rate**

 
 
• Exponential growth occurs when the growth rate of a mathematical function's value is proportional to the function's current value.
 
• In the context of population, it means the population grows at a constant percentage rate per period.
 
• The formula for exponential growth is *P(t) = P₀ * ert*, where:
 
 
• *P(t)* is the future population.
 
• *P₀* is the initial population.
 
• *r* is the growth rate.
 
• *t* is the time period.
 
• *e* is the base of the natural logarithm, approximately equal to 2.71828.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Census**
 
 
• A census is a systematic enumeration of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• The Census of India is a decennial (every 10 years) exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• It provides vital data on population size, distribution, and various demographic characteristics.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.
